sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Kirkland, WA?
sections.html:
A Kirkland owner has three routes: list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who pays without a mortgage. The cash route removes loan approval and usually the repair list, which is why it is the quickest of the three. Every route still ends at the same Washington closing items: excise tax, prorated property tax and a completed seller disclosure statement.

Kirkland is an expensive place to own a home, and that shapes the decision. The Census Bureau reports a median value of owner-occupied housing of $1,115,400 for 2020 to 2024, with 60.8 percent of homes owner-occupied. At those values, the graduated state excise tax and the carrying cost of an empty house both matter, so a shorter timeline can be worth real money.

sections.h2: What is Kirkland like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Kirkland sits on the eastern shore of Lake Washington, and its downtown wraps around Moss Bay with restaurants, galleries, parks and a large stock of condominiums built since the 1990s. Interstate 405 links it to Bellevue, Renton and Bothell, and State Route 520 reaches Seattle and Redmond. The city covers 17.81 square miles of land and ranges from 14 to 500 feet above sea level.

The city was incorporated in 1905, merged with the neighboring town of Houghton in 1968, and grew through annexations. Totem Lake joined in 1974, South Juanita and the Rose Hill areas in 1988, and Finn Hill, North Juanita and Kingsgate on June 1, 2011, which added about 33,000 residents. A house in one of those areas can have a very different lot, age and street pattern from one near Moss Bay, so a buyer or appraiser will compare it against its own neighborhood.

  • Moss Bay and downtown: condominiums, apartments and the waterfront.
  • Houghton: where the first homesteads went up in the late 1860s.
  • Rose Hill: the hill where a steel mill was finished in 1892, with North and South Rose Hill annexed in 1988.
  • Totem Lake: annexed in 1974 and served by Sound Transit and Community Transit buses on I-405.
  • Juanita, Finn Hill and Kingsgate: the northern neighborhoods, with Finn Hill, North Juanita and Kingsgate annexed in 2011.

Most of Kirkland is in the Lake Washington School District, with Juanita High School and Lake Washington High School inside the city. Smaller parts fall in the Bellevue and Northshore districts. Evergreen Healthcare, Google and the school district were the three largest local employers in 2023.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees does a Kirkland seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
The seller normally pays Washington real estate excise tax, and it is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The Department of Revenue says an unpaid tax can become a lien on the property, and interest runs if it is not paid within one month of the sale date. A local excise tax set by the city is added to the state portion, so ask your escrow officer for the combined figure on your parcel.

The state portion is graduated under RCW 82.45.060. The Department of Revenue lists these thresholds for sales beginning January 1, 2027:

  • 1.1 percent on the part of the price up to $551,000.
  • 1.28 percent on the part from $551,000 to $1,551,000.
  • 2.75 percent on the part from $1,551,000 to $3,051,000.
  • 3 percent on anything above $3,051,000.

As an illustration, a $1,200,000 sale closing in 2027 would owe $6,061 on the first slice and $8,307 on the next $649,000, about $14,368 in state tax before the local portion. Sales that close before January 1, 2027 use the earlier thresholds, which your escrow officer will apply. Details are on the Department of Revenue excise tax page.

sections.h2: When are King County property taxes due on a Kirkland home?
sections.html:
King County property tax is due in two halves, on April 30 and October 31. The second-half 2026 date has already passed, and the next first-half payment is due April 30, 2027. The King County Treasury takes payment online, by mail with a postmark on or before the due date, in person at 201 S. Jackson Street in Seattle, or at a drop box at the same building.

When a Kirkland house sells mid-year, the escrow officer prorates the bill between you and the buyer, so confirm that your last payment has posted before closing. The Treasury has posted a notice that processing of some second-half 2026 payments was delayed, and it asks owners to check the online portal to confirm their account was credited. Seniors, people with disabilities and some disabled veterans may qualify for exemption or deferral programs, which the King County Assessor administers.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Kirkland house that has tenants or a short-term rental license?
sections.html:
Yes, but Kirkland treats rentals as a business activity. The city requires a business license for any long-term or short-term rental, and operating without one can be a misdemeanor. A buyer who plans to keep the rental will ask for the license history, so have it ready.

Short-term rentals (under 30 days) fall under Ordinance O-4607, and the city's page lists the main limits for single-family homes:

  • An owner or agent who lives in the home continuously may rent short-term with no day cap, up to two rentals at a time.
  • An owner or agent present at least 245 days a year may rent short-term up to 120 days a year.
  • When no one is home, a property manager within 15 miles must be named to the city.
  • Parking is one stall per rental, plus two more stalls if permanent residents live in the home.

The city lists a $100 base fee plus a $130 per-employee regulatory fee for the business license, or $230 for many short-term rentals. Kirkland charges no business and occupation tax. A condominium is generally outside these rules, but the association's own rules still apply. Owners are responsible for lodging tax under state law.

sections.h2: Does Kirkland's weather affect when to sell?
sections.html:
Kirkland averages 36.27 inches of precipitation a year, with the wettest months being November at 5.84 inches, December at 5.43 inches and January at 4.81 inches. Summer is dry, with July averaging 0.79 inches. The record high of 109 degrees came on June 28, 2021, and snow averages 8.1 inches a year.

A winter buyer inspection happens in the wettest weather, so roof, gutter and drainage problems show up quickly. If you are fixing anything, finish those items before listing. If you are selling as-is to a cash buyer, the schedule does not depend on the season.

sections.h2: What must a Kirkland seller disclose?
sections.html:
Washington requires the seller of improved residential property to deliver a completed disclosure statement unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt, under RCW 64.06.020. The form asks about sewer or septic, roof leaks in the last five years, structural issues, and environmental concerns such as lead-based paint or storage tanks. It covers what you actually know, and the buyer has three business days from delivery to rescind unless both sides agree otherwise in writing.

Answer every line, and write NA where a question does not apply. An incomplete form invites disputes later, whether the buyer is financing or paying cash.

faqs.q: How fast can a Kirkland house sell for cash?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close faster than a financed sale because no lender approval is required, and timing is set by title work and the closing date you choose. The county treasurer must still receive excise tax and the deed must be recorded.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax in Kirkland?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays it, according to the Department of Revenue, and if the seller does not, the buyer becomes responsible. The tax is due to the King County treasurer on the date of sale, with interest if unpaid after one month.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent my Kirkland house before selling?
faqs.a: Yes. Kirkland requires a city business license for long-term and short-term rentals, and short-term rentals also need a state license. Operating without one can be a misdemeanor, so settle that before a buyer reviews your rental records.

faqs.q: Are King County property taxes still due if I am selling?
faqs.a: Yes, until closing. Payments are due April 30 and October 31, and the escrow officer prorates the bill at closing. Check the Treasury's online portal to confirm your payment posted.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Kirkland?
faqs.a: Yes, it can be sold once the person with legal authority to sign the deed is in place. Ask a Washington estate attorney or your title company who that is, and note that a deed transfer still goes with an excise tax affidavit to the King County treasurer.
